title: Ars Live: What drone attacks on data centers mean for modern life in the cloud
gist: Event announcement for an Ars Live discussion with RUSI's Joseph Jarnecki on drone and missile strikes against data centers, which in 2026 disrupted cloud services in Eastern Europe and the Middle East and permanently deleted some AWS customer data. Light on new analysis; mainly recaps prior reporting.

insights.claim: Drone and missile strikes in 2026 have inflicted unprecedented damage on data centers in Eastern Europe and the Middle East, disrupting cloud services for millions and permanently deleting some Amazon Web Services customer data.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: Physical war risk is now a real loss event for hyperscaler customers, affecting cloud siting, insurance and redundancy costs.
insights.quote: permanently deleting some Amazon Web Services customer data

insights.claim: Iran's drone and missile strikes on Amazon data centers in the Middle East during the US-Israeli war with Iran left Amazon facing months of repairs.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: Regional hyperscaler expansion in the Gulf carries kinetic risk that may weigh on capex plans and SLAs there.
insights.locator: For more background on the data center attacks

insights.claim: A systematic Russian strike campaign on Ukraine's data centers provoked Ukrainian counterstrikes that damaged Russian government data centers and AI data centers owned by Yandex.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: Data center attacks escalate symmetrically, making AI infrastructure of both sides a target.
insights.locator: I’ve also covered why Russia was not ready

insights.claim: The article frames data center attacks as a new concern not only for Big Tech but for governments and everyone dependent on common digital services.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: Raises the case for sovereign cloud, geographic redundancy and data center hardening spending.

insights.claim: RUSI senior research fellow Joseph Jarnecki has researched how Ukraine strengthened its cloud resilience with Western partners despite cyberattacks and kinetic attacks at the start of Russia's full-scale invasion, and what that means for NATO and European government cloud adoption.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: Ukraine's model of offshoring state data to Western cloud informs European defense cloud procurement.

insights.claim: Open questions for governments and cloud providers include whether hardening data centers against drones and missiles is realistic and how to deploy data centers amid growing geopolitical risk.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: Hardening and siting choices could add cost to data center buildouts in contested regions.
insights.locator: My conversation with Jarnecki will explore
